title: How to Find Direction in God
shortDescription: Finding direction in God is not only about knowing what decision to make, but discerning where He is shaping and sending your life. Over six days, you will explore how identity, the Word, desires, gifts, character, community, and obedience work together to shape a calling. This plan will help you seek direction without superstition, without anxiety, and without waiting for absolute certainty before moving forward.
learning: Understand God's direction as part of the process of discovering and living out purpose
Use the Word as a framework for evaluating decisions and possibilities
Examine desires, gifts, and burdens without automatically turning them into callings
Recognize the role of character and priorities in discernment
Value community and external confirmation without depending on human approval
Learn to obey with the clarity available while purpose continues to take shape
gains: Greater clarity for connecting present decisions with purpose
Less dependence on ambiguous signs or momentary emotions
More discernment for evaluating desires, opportunities, and abilities
A more mature view of how God confirms and directs a calling
Greater freedom to move forward without having all the answers
A more stable way to make decisions with faith, wisdom, and obedience

days.title: Direction Begins by Understanding Who You Live For
days.text:
When we seek direction, we often begin by asking which option benefits us most. But the Bible leads us to a deeper question: who are you living for? The answer changes the way you evaluate decisions.

Paul teaches that our lives belong to the Lord. Colossians invites us to do everything in the name of Jesus. This means direction is not limited to choosing between two paths; it also involves deciding what kind of life you want to offer to God.

One option may seem attractive and still lead you away from the values you want to live by. Another may be less impressive but more aligned with service, integrity, and obedience. Finding direction begins when purpose stops being only “what do I want to do?” and becomes “how do I want to live before God?”
days.internalize: Before evaluating options, define the center: “I want my life to be oriented toward God, not only toward what is most convenient for me.”
days.prayer: Lord, order my decisions around You. Help me not to seek direction only from my preferences, but from the desire to live in a way that honors You. Amen.
days.action: Write down three biblical values you want every important decision to respect, regardless of which option you choose.

days.title: The Word Defines the Ground of Discernment
days.text:
Not every direction requires an extraordinary revelation. Many decisions can begin to become clearer when the Word establishes boundaries, priorities, and criteria.

Scripture renews the mind, corrects, and equips. It will not always tell you which company to join, which city to choose, or which project to start, but it does form the kind of person who can evaluate those options wisely.

God's direction never needs to contradict what He has already revealed about truth, justice, love, responsibility, and holiness. If an opportunity requires abandoning clear principles, you do not need an additional sign to justify it.

The Word does not always eliminate every option, but it does help you recognize which paths are not consistent with a life of purpose.
days.internalize: Ask: “Does this decision allow me to live according to what God has already shown in his Word?”
days.prayer: Father, thank You for your Word. Renew the way I think and give me a heart willing to obey what You have already made clear before I ask for new answers. Amen.
days.action: Take one pending decision and write down which biblical principles should influence it. Eliminate any option that clearly contradicts them.

days.title: Your Desires and Gifts Can Guide You, but They Need to Be Examined
days.text:
God can use desires, abilities, and experiences to guide your life. What you do well, the needs that move you, and the places where others recognize fruit can offer important clues.

But a clue is not a verdict. We can desire something because of comparison, fear, or the need for approval. We can also have a gift that is useful in more than one context. That is why discernment requires looking at both ability and motivation.

Peter teaches us to use our gifts to serve. That idea offers a valuable question: how can what you have received become good for others? When desire, ability, and service begin to come together, a clearer direction may emerge.
days.internalize: Do not turn a desire into a calling too quickly. Examine whether there is also ability, fruit, and a real opportunity to serve.
days.prayer: God, thank You for the desires and gifts You have allowed in my life. Purify my motives and help me recognize how I can use what I have received to serve with humility. Amen.
days.action: Write down three areas that interest you and, beside each one, answer: Do I have ability? Is there fruit? Can it serve others?

days.title: Character Also Shows Whether a Direction Is Mature
days.text:
We can become obsessed with finding the right opportunity and overlook whether our character is ready to sustain it. The Bible gives great attention to who we are, not only to what we do.

The fruit of the Spirit shows qualities that affect every calling: patience, self-control, kindness, and faithfulness. A direction may seem right and still reveal areas that need more formation before greater responsibility is taken on.

This does not mean waiting until you are perfect. It means allowing discernment to include an honest evaluation. Perhaps the next step is not gaining more visibility, but developing discipline, healing a motivation, or learning to manage a current responsibility better.

Sometimes God directs by forming before sending.
days.internalize: Ask: “What part of my character needs to grow in order to sustain well the direction I desire?”
days.prayer: Lord, do not let me pursue opportunities faster than I am willing to grow. Form in me the character needed to faithfully steward what You place in my hands. Amen.
days.action: Choose one character quality that would be essential for the direction you are considering and define one concrete practice to strengthen it this week.

days.title: Community Can Confirm What You Are Only Beginning to See
days.text:
There are aspects of our calling that other people may recognize before we do. In Acts, the community participated in discernment and sending. The Bible also highlights the value of counsel and the different members of the body.

A healthy community can confirm gifts, observe fruit, and point out blind spots. It can tell you, “We see grace in you here,” or “This motivation needs to be examined.” That kind of support protects us from isolation and from the tendency to interpret every personal desire as divine direction.

But confirmation should not become dependence. No one can live your obedience for you. Counsel brings perspective; you are still responsible for discerning before God.

Mature direction listens to wise voices without handing them control of the calling.
days.internalize: Think about what mature people have consistently observed in your life, not just isolated opinions.
days.prayer: Father, thank You for the people who can help me discern. Give me humility to listen, freedom from dependence on approval, and wisdom to recognize healthy confirmation. Amen.
days.action: Ask two mature people where they see fruit, ability, or calling in your life. Look for patterns in their answers, not phrases that simply confirm what you already want.

days.title: Direction Becomes Clearer When You Obey
days.text:
There comes a point when continuing to think no longer produces clarity. After praying, evaluating, listening, and examining your heart, the time comes to move.

Abraham left without knowing every detail. Proverbs acknowledges that we plan while God directs. Psalm 37 speaks of established steps. The biblical picture of discernment includes movement.

Obedience does not mean having absolute certainty. It means moving forward with the best clarity available while remaining willing to adjust. If a door changes, you can reevaluate. If new information appears, you can adapt. God does not stop guiding you after the first step.

Direction in purpose is often discovered along a path, not in a single revelation. One faithful step today can show you something that was impossible to see while standing still.
days.internalize: Close this journey with this decision: “I will not wait for perfect certainty to obey what already seems wise, biblical, and consistent with the purpose God is forming.”
days.prayer: Lord, give me courage to walk with the clarity I have. Establish my steps, correct me when necessary, and keep my heart open to your direction as I move forward. Amen.
days.action: Define one concrete step for the next seven days that aligns with what you have discerned. Give it a date and carry it out without requiring it to solve your entire future.
